## The arithmetic hands-on {#arithmetic-route}

This section builds one floating-point lowering step by step.

::: {.incremental}
1. **Exercise 6:** lower integer `arith.muli` into `hw` and `comb`.

2. **Exercise 7:** construct an E4M3 multiplier.

3. **Exercise 8 (optional):** recognize squaring and build a cheaper datapath.
:::

## Exercise 6: start from generic MLIR {#arithmetic-objective}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
```bash
cat examples/ex6_arith_muli.mlir
```

<div class="code-gap"></div>

```mlir
module {
  func.func @ex6_mul(%a : i8, %b : i8) -> i8 {
    %r = arith.muli %a, %b : i8
    return %r : i8
  }
}
```
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.fragment}
**Objective: a combinational hardware module**

```mlir
hw.module @ex6_mul(
    in %in0 : i8, in %in1 : i8, out out0 : i8) {
  %0 = comb.mul %in0, %in1 : i8
  hw.output %0 : i8
}
```

This is the smallest complete path to SystemVerilog and logic synthesis.
:::
:::
::::

## Exercise 6: find the missing passes - 3 min {#arithmetic-exercise-6}

To reach that objective, two things must change:

- `func.func` and `return` must become a hardware module boundary.
- `arith.muli` must become a combinational multiplier.

Does upstream `circt-opt` provide both transformations?

```bash
circt-opt --help | grep -i arith
circt-opt --help | grep -i func
```

:::: {.columns .fragment}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Relevant `arith` result**

```text
--convert-comb-to-arith
--lower-hwarith-to-hw
--map-arith-to-comb
```
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
**Relevant `func` result**

```text
--lower-cf-to-handshake
    Lower func and CF into Handshake IR
```

No direct generic `func.func` → `hw.module` pass.
:::
::::

## Exercise 6: compose two passes {#arithmetic-integer-pipeline}

```bash
circt-tutorial-opt examples/ex6_arith_muli.mlir \
  --tutorial-func-to-hw -o build/ex6_hw_arith.mlir

circt-opt build/ex6_hw_arith.mlir \
  --map-arith-to-comb -o build/ex6_hw_comb.mlir
```

| File | Boundary | Multiplication |
|---|---|---|
| `ex6_arith_muli.mlir` | `func.func` | `arith.muli` |
| `ex6_hw_arith.mlir` | `hw.module` | `arith.muli` |
| `ex6_hw_comb.mlir` | `hw.module` | `comb.mul` |

**Boundary first; multiplication second.**

## `map-arith-to-comb` draws a deliberate line {#arithmetic-map-contract}

```{.text code-line-numbers="2,4|5-6|9-13"}
def MapArithToCombPass : Pass<"map-arith-to-comb"> {
  let summary = "Map arith ops to combinational logic";
  let description = [{
    A pass which does a simple `arith` to `comb` mapping wherever possible.
    This pass will not convert:
    * floating point operations
    * operations using `vector`-typed values

    This does not intend to be the definitive lowering/HLS pass of `arith`
    operations in CIRCT (hence the name "map" instead of e.g. "lower").
    Rather, it provides a simple way (mostly for testing purposes) to map
    `arith` operations.
  }];
}
```

[CIRCT `Transforms/Passes.td`, pinned `firtool-1.147.0` source](https://github.com/llvm/circt/blob/firtool-1.147.0/include/circt/Transforms/Passes.td#L56-L76)

The failure is the documented boundary of the pass. Our exercise supplies one
concrete floating-point lowering.

## Read the type name: `f8E4M3FN` {#arithmetic-e4m3-name}

| Part | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `f8` | 8-bit floating-point type |
| `E4` | 4 exponent bits |
| `M3` | 3 stored mantissa/fraction bits |
| `FN` | **F = finite; N = NaN.** No infinity encoding. |

Overflow therefore produces NaN instead of infinity.

[MLIR Builtin floating-point types](https://mlir.llvm.org/docs/Dialects/Builtin/#types)

## Eight bits encode several numerical regimes {#arithmetic-e4m3-format}

::: {.bit-layout}
::: {.bit-field .sign}
**s**

`[7]`

<small>sign · 1 bit</small>
:::
::: {.bit-field .exponent}
**eeee**

`[6:3]`

<small>biased exponent · 4 bits</small>
:::
::: {.bit-field .fraction}
**mmm**

`[2:0]`

<small>stored fraction · 3 bits</small>
:::
:::

| Regime | Encoding | Value |
|---|---|---|
| zero | `e = 0000`, `m = 000` | $0$ |
| subnormal | `e = 0000`, `m != 000` | $(-1)^s 2^{-6}(m/8)$ |
| normal | `e != 0000` | $(-1)^s 2^{e-7}(1+m/8)$ |
| NaN | `e = 1111`, `m = 111` | not a number |

`f8E4M3FN` has bias 7, finite values up to 448, and no infinity.
[@micikevicius2022fp8]

## Normal binades double; subnormals fill the gap {#arithmetic-e4m3-axis}

A binade $[2^k,2^{k+1})$ contains the values that share one exponent.

::: {.r-stack}
![](assets/images/e4m3-binades.svg){fig-alt="Normal E4M3FN binades double in width and leave no normal values between zero and two to the minus six" width="94%"}

![](assets/images/e4m3-binades-subnormals.svg){.fragment data-fragment-index="0" fig-alt="Seven subnormal values fill the interval next to zero" width="94%"}
:::

::: {.fragment data-fragment-index="0"}
Subnormals make underflow **gradual**: seven values continue the smallest normal
spacing toward zero, preserving nearby subtraction (Sterbenz's lemma).
:::

::: {.fragment data-fragment-index="1"}
**Exercise 7 keeps only the normal path.** Many accelerators choose flush-to-zero:
less shifting and control for AI workloads that tolerate tiny perturbations.
:::

## The same format spans tiny values to 448 {#arithmetic-e4m3-values}

| Hex | Fields `s eeee mmm` | Value |
|---:|---|---:|
| `0x00` | `0 0000 000` | 0 |
| `0x08` | `0 0001 000` | $2^{-6}$ |
| `0x30` | `0 0110 000` | 0.5 |
| `0x38` | `0 0111 000` | 1 |
| `0x3C` | `0 0111 100` | 1.5 |
| `0x41` | `0 1000 001` | 2.25 |
| `0x7E` | `0 1111 110` | 448 |
| `0x7F` | `0 1111 111` | NaN |

Less precision buys a smaller representation and more operations per watt;
the exact rounding and exceptional-value rules remain part of the contract.

## Exercise 7: build an E4M3 multiplier {#arithmetic-pass-goal data-transition="none"}

:::: {.e4m3-rewrite-layout}
::: {.e4m3-diagram-panel}
<div class="r-stack e4m3-vertical-stack" data-id="e4m3-datapath">

```mlir
%bf = arith.bitcast %b : i8 to f8E4M3FN
%p = arith.mulf %af, %bf : f8E4M3FN
%r = arith.bitcast %p : f8E4M3FN to i8
```

Root the rewrite at the final `arith.bitcast`: the matched island and its
replacement then have the same `i8` boundary.

```python-circt
    matched = match_e4m3_island(out_cast)  # supplied
    if matched is None:
        return True
    lhs, rhs = matched
    with rewriter.ip:
        ...
    rewriter.replace_op(out_cast, [result])
    return False

patterns.add(
    arith.BitcastOp, lower_e4m3_mul)
```
:::

## What must the circuit compute? {#arithmetic-mult-decomposition data-transition="none"}

:::: {.e4m3-rewrite-layout}
::: {.e4m3-diagram-panel}
<div class="r-stack e4m3-vertical-stack" data-id="e4m3-datapath">
  <img data-id="e4m3-base" src="assets/images/arithmetic/e4m3-rewrite-base.svg" alt="Two E4M3 inputs above an empty multiplier datapath">
  <img data-id="e4m3-question" src="assets/images/arithmetic/e4m3-rewrite-question.svg" alt="Unknown E4M3 multiplier implementation">
</div>
:::

::: {.e4m3-rewrite-copy data-id="e4m3-copy"}
For a normal, finite value, let $E$ be the stored exponent, $B=7$, and $M$ the
significand:

$$x=(-1)^s\,2^{E-B}\,M,
\qquad M=(1.\mathtt{mmm})_2$$

Multiplying two values exposes the three datapaths we must build:

$$ab=
\underbrace{(-1)^{s_a\oplus s_b}}_{\text{sign}}
\;\underbrace{2^{(E_a-B)+(E_b-B)}}_{\text{exponent}}
\;\underbrace{(M_aM_b)}_{\text{significand}}$$

The significand product may need normalization; that correction is then added
to the result exponent.
:::
::::

## Together: route the sign {#arithmetic-sign-path data-transition="none"}

:::: {.e4m3-rewrite-layout}
::: {.e4m3-diagram-panel}
<div class="r-stack e4m3-vertical-stack" data-id="e4m3-datapath">
  <img data-id="e4m3-base" src="assets/images/arithmetic/e4m3-rewrite-base.svg" alt="E4M3 multiplier datapath">
  <img data-id="e4m3-sign" src="assets/images/arithmetic/e4m3-rewrite-sign.svg" alt="" aria-hidden="true">
</div>
:::

::: {.e4m3-rewrite-copy data-id="e4m3-copy"}
<div class="e4m3-stage-cue stage-sign">First: compute the sign.</div>

::: {.e4m3-stage-math .stage-sign}
$$(-1)^{s_a}(-1)^{s_b}=(-1)^{s_a+s_b}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad s_r=s_a\oplus s_b$$
:::

**First make the rewrite compile.** Extract both signs, XOR them, and set the
remaining seven output bits to zero.

::: {.e4m3-stage-code .stage-sign}
**Sign path**

```python-circt
sa = comb.ExtractOp.create(7, i1, lhs).result
sb = comb.ExtractOp.create(7, i1, rhs).result
sign = comb.XorOp.create(sa, sb).result

zero7 = hw.ConstantOp.create(i7, 0).result
result = comb.ConcatOp.create(sign, zero7).result
```
:::

The long purple wire is now a real SSA value from both inputs to the packed
result.
:::
::::

## Worked example: cumulative sign path {#arithmetic-sign-recap data-transition="none"}

:::: {.e4m3-rewrite-layout}
::: {.e4m3-diagram-panel .e4m3-recap-panel}
<div class="e4m3-recap-caption">Cumulative schematic</div>
<div class="r-stack e4m3-vertical-stack" data-id="e4m3-datapath">
  <img data-id="e4m3-base" src="assets/images/arithmetic/e4m3-rewrite-base.svg" alt="E4M3 multiplier datapath">
  <img data-id="e4m3-sign" src="assets/images/arithmetic/e4m3-rewrite-sign.svg" alt="" aria-hidden="true">
</div>
:::

::: {.e4m3-rewrite-copy .e4m3-function-recap .e4m3-recap-panel data-id="e4m3-copy"}
<div class="e4m3-recap-caption">Cumulative Python lowering</div>
```python-circt
def lower_e4m3_mul(out_cast, rewriter):
    matched = match_e4m3_island(out_cast)
    if matched is None:
        return True
    lhs, rhs = matched
    with rewriter.ip:
        sa = comb.ExtractOp.create(7, i1, lhs).result
        sb = comb.ExtractOp.create(7, i1, rhs).result
        sign = comb.XorOp.create(sa, sb).result
        zero7 = hw.ConstantOp.create(i7, 0).result
        result = comb.ConcatOp.create(sign, zero7).result
    rewriter.replace_op(out_cast, [result])
    return False
```
:::

## Exercise 7A: multiply the significands - 6 min {#arithmetic-exercise-7a data-transition="none"}

:::: {.e4m3-rewrite-layout}
::: {.e4m3-diagram-panel}
<div class="r-stack e4m3-vertical-stack" data-id="e4m3-datapath">
  <img data-id="e4m3-base" src="assets/images/arithmetic/e4m3-rewrite-base.svg" alt="E4M3 multiplier with its sign path completed">
  <img data-id="e4m3-sign" src="assets/images/arithmetic/e4m3-rewrite-sign.svg" alt="" aria-hidden="true">
  <img data-id="e4m3-significand-question" src="assets/images/arithmetic/e4m3-rewrite-significand-question.svg" alt="The significand product is the next datapath to implement">
</div>
:::

::: {.e4m3-rewrite-copy data-id="e4m3-copy"}
<div class="e4m3-stage-cue stage-significand">Now: multiply the significands.</div>

Normalized scientific notation keeps one non-zero digit before the point. In
binary that digit can only be `1`, so every normal significand is `1.mmm₂`.
Because this leading `1` is predictable, E4M3 stores only `mmm`.

::: {.e4m3-stage-math .stage-significand}
$$M=1+\frac{(\mathtt{mmm})_2}{2^3}=(1.\mathtt{mmm})_2,
\qquad \boxed{P=M_aM_b}$$
:::

**Your step:** prepend the implicit `1`, form both 4-bit significands, then
produce the full-width `%product : i8`. `comb.mul` returns the operand width.
:::
::::

## Exercise 7A: solution {#arithmetic-exercise-7a-solution data-transition="none"}

:::: {.e4m3-rewrite-layout}
::: {.e4m3-diagram-panel}
<div class="r-stack e4m3-vertical-stack" data-id="e4m3-datapath">
  <img data-id="e4m3-base" src="assets/images/arithmetic/e4m3-rewrite-base.svg" alt="E4M3 multiplier with its significand product completed">
  <img data-id="e4m3-sign" src="assets/images/arithmetic/e4m3-rewrite-sign.svg" alt="" aria-hidden="true">
  <img data-id="e4m3-significand" src="assets/images/arithmetic/e4m3-rewrite-significand.svg" alt="" aria-hidden="true">
</div>
:::

::: {.e4m3-rewrite-copy data-id="e4m3-copy"}
<div class="e4m3-stage-cue stage-significand">Now: multiply the significands.</div>

Reconstruct `1.mmm₂`, zero-extend both 4-bit significands to the result width,
then multiply them as integers.

::: {.e4m3-stage-math .stage-significand}
$$M=1+\frac{(\mathtt{mmm})_2}{2^3}=(1.\mathtt{mmm})_2,
\qquad P=M_aM_b$$
:::

::: {.e4m3-stage-code .stage-significand}
**Solution**

```python-circt
fa = comb.ExtractOp.create(0, i3, lhs).result
fb = comb.ExtractOp.create(0, i3, rhs).result
one = hw.ConstantOp.create(i1, 1).result
ma4 = comb.ConcatOp.create(one, fa).result
mb4 = comb.ConcatOp.create(one, fb).result
zero4 = hw.ConstantOp.create(i4, 0).result
ma8 = comb.ConcatOp.create(zero4, ma4).result
mb8 = comb.ConcatOp.create(zero4, mb4).result
product = comb.MulOp.create(ma8, mb8).result
```
:::
:::
::::

## Exercise 7A: cumulative implementation {#arithmetic-significand-recap data-transition="none"}

:::: {.e4m3-rewrite-layout}
::: {.e4m3-diagram-panel .e4m3-recap-panel}
<div class="e4m3-recap-caption">Cumulative schematic</div>
<div class="r-stack e4m3-vertical-stack" data-id="e4m3-datapath">
  <img data-id="e4m3-base" src="assets/images/arithmetic/e4m3-rewrite-base.svg" alt="E4M3 multiplier with its significand product completed">
  <img data-id="e4m3-sign" src="assets/images/arithmetic/e4m3-rewrite-sign.svg" alt="" aria-hidden="true">
  <img data-id="e4m3-significand" src="assets/images/arithmetic/e4m3-rewrite-significand.svg" alt="" aria-hidden="true">
</div>
:::

::: {.e4m3-rewrite-copy .e4m3-function-recap .e4m3-recap-panel data-id="e4m3-copy"}
<div class="e4m3-recap-caption">Cumulative Python lowering</div>
```python-circt
def lower_e4m3_mul(out_cast, rewriter):
    matched = match_e4m3_island(out_cast)
    if matched is None:
        return True
    lhs, rhs = matched
    with rewriter.ip:
        sa = comb.ExtractOp.create(7, i1, lhs).result
        sb = comb.ExtractOp.create(7, i1, rhs).result
        sign = comb.XorOp.create(sa, sb).result
        fa = comb.ExtractOp.create(0, i3, lhs).result
        fb = comb.ExtractOp.create(0, i3, rhs).result
        one = hw.ConstantOp.create(i1, 1).result
        ma4 = comb.ConcatOp.create(one, fa).result
        mb4 = comb.ConcatOp.create(one, fb).result
        zero4 = hw.ConstantOp.create(i4, 0).result
        ma8 = comb.ConcatOp.create(zero4, ma4).result
        mb8 = comb.ConcatOp.create(zero4, mb4).result
        product = comb.MulOp.create(ma8, mb8).result
        zero7 = hw.ConstantOp.create(i7, 0).result
        result = comb.ConcatOp.create(sign, zero7).result
    rewriter.replace_op(out_cast, [result])
    return False
```
:::
::::

## One bit chooses the normalization {#arithmetic-normalization-bit data-transition="none"}

:::: {.e4m3-rewrite-layout}
::: {.e4m3-diagram-panel}
<div class="r-stack e4m3-vertical-stack" data-id="e4m3-datapath">
  <img data-id="e4m3-base" src="assets/images/arithmetic/e4m3-rewrite-base.svg" alt="E4M3 multiplier through the full significand product">
  <img data-id="e4m3-sign" src="assets/images/arithmetic/e4m3-rewrite-sign.svg" alt="" aria-hidden="true">
  <img data-id="e4m3-significand" src="assets/images/arithmetic/e4m3-rewrite-significand.svg" alt="" aria-hidden="true">
</div>
:::

::: {.e4m3-rewrite-copy data-id="e4m3-copy"}
<div class="e4m3-stage-cue stage-normalize">Next: normalize the product.</div>

Each reconstructed significand is in $[1,2)$, so their product is in $[1,4)$.
Only two leading forms are possible:

::: {.e4m3-normal-table}
| Product form | Test | Keep | Exponent |
|---|---:|---|---:|
| `1.xxxxxx₂` | `%product[7] = 0` | `%product[6:3]` | `+ 0` |
| `10.xxxxx₂` | `%product[7] = 1` | `%product[7:4]` | `+ 1` |
:::

The `10.x…₂` case has two bits before the binary point; normalized form allows
only `1.x…₂`:

::: {.e4m3-stage-math .stage-normalize}
$$1.100_2 \times 1.100_2 = 10.010000_2 = 1.001000_2 \times 2^1$$
:::

The shift restores `1.x…₂`; incrementing the exponent preserves the value.
Thus `0x3C × 0x3C` produces `0x41` ($2.25$).
:::
::::

## Exercise 7B: build the normalization mux - 7 min {#arithmetic-exercise-7b data-transition="none"}

:::: {.e4m3-rewrite-layout}
::: {.e4m3-diagram-panel}
<div class="r-stack e4m3-vertical-stack" data-id="e4m3-datapath">
  <img data-id="e4m3-base" src="assets/images/arithmetic/e4m3-rewrite-base.svg" alt="E4M3 multiplier before normalization">
  <img data-id="e4m3-sign" src="assets/images/arithmetic/e4m3-rewrite-sign.svg" alt="" aria-hidden="true">
  <img data-id="e4m3-significand" src="assets/images/arithmetic/e4m3-rewrite-significand.svg" alt="" aria-hidden="true">
</div>
:::

::: {.e4m3-rewrite-copy data-id="e4m3-copy"}
::: {.e4m3-stage-math .stage-normalize}
$$n=\begin{cases}0 & P<2\\1 & P\ge 2\end{cases}
\qquad M_r=P\,2^{-n}$$
:::

The bit `%product[7]` distinguishes `1.x…` from `10.x…`. Use it to select the
normalized window, then retain it as the exponent correction.

**Your step:** produce `%frac : i3` and retain `%norm : i1` for the exponent.
:::
::::

## Exercise 7B: solution {#arithmetic-exercise-7b-solution data-transition="none"}

:::: {.e4m3-rewrite-layout}
::: {.e4m3-diagram-panel}
<div class="r-stack e4m3-vertical-stack" data-id="e4m3-datapath">
  <img data-id="e4m3-base" src="assets/images/arithmetic/e4m3-rewrite-base.svg" alt="E4M3 multiplier with normalization completed">
  <img data-id="e4m3-sign" src="assets/images/arithmetic/e4m3-rewrite-sign.svg" alt="" aria-hidden="true">
  <img data-id="e4m3-significand" src="assets/images/arithmetic/e4m3-rewrite-significand.svg" alt="" aria-hidden="true">
  <img data-id="e4m3-normalize" src="assets/images/arithmetic/e4m3-rewrite-normalize.svg" alt="" aria-hidden="true">
</div>
:::

::: {.e4m3-rewrite-copy data-id="e4m3-copy"}
::: {.e4m3-stage-math .stage-normalize}
$$n=\begin{cases}0 & P<2\\1 & P\ge 2\end{cases}
\qquad M_r=P\,2^{-n}$$
:::

The bit `%product[7]` distinguishes `1.x…` from `10.x…`. Use it to select the
normalized window, then retain it as the exponent correction.

::: {.e4m3-stage-code .stage-normalize}
**Solution**

```python-circt
norm = comb.ExtractOp.create(7, i1, product).result
direct = comb.ExtractOp.create(3, i4, product).result
shifted = comb.ExtractOp.create(4, i4, product).result
mant = comb.MuxOp.create(norm, shifted, direct).result
frac = comb.ExtractOp.create(0, i3, mant).result
```

```python-circt
def lower_e4m3_mul(out_cast, rewriter):
    matched = match_e4m3_island(out_cast)
    if matched is None:
        return True
    lhs, rhs = matched
    with rewriter.ip:
        sa = comb.ExtractOp.create(7, i1, lhs).result
        sb = comb.ExtractOp.create(7, i1, rhs).result
        sign = comb.XorOp.create(sa, sb).result
        fa = comb.ExtractOp.create(0, i3, lhs).result
        fb = comb.ExtractOp.create(0, i3, rhs).result
        one = hw.ConstantOp.create(i1, 1).result
        ma4 = comb.ConcatOp.create(one, fa).result
        mb4 = comb.ConcatOp.create(one, fb).result
        zero4 = hw.ConstantOp.create(i4, 0).result
        ma8 = comb.ConcatOp.create(zero4, ma4).result
        mb8 = comb.ConcatOp.create(zero4, mb4).result
        product = comb.MulOp.create(ma8, mb8).result
        norm = comb.ExtractOp.create(7, i1, product).result
        direct = comb.ExtractOp.create(3, i4, product).result
        shifted = comb.ExtractOp.create(4, i4, product).result
        mant = comb.MuxOp.create(norm, shifted, direct).result
        frac = comb.ExtractOp.create(0, i3, mant).result
        result = comb.ConcatOp.create(sign, zero4, frac).result
    rewriter.replace_op(out_cast, [result])
    return False
```

## Why subtract only one bias? {#arithmetic-exponent-math data-transition="none"}

:::: {.e4m3-rewrite-layout}
::: {.e4m3-diagram-panel}
<div class="r-stack e4m3-vertical-stack" data-id="e4m3-datapath">
  <img data-id="e4m3-base" src="assets/images/arithmetic/e4m3-rewrite-base.svg" alt="E4M3 multiplier before exponent adjustment">
  <img data-id="e4m3-sign" src="assets/images/arithmetic/e4m3-rewrite-sign.svg" alt="" aria-hidden="true">
  <img data-id="e4m3-significand" src="assets/images/arithmetic/e4m3-rewrite-significand.svg" alt="" aria-hidden="true">
  <img data-id="e4m3-normalize" src="assets/images/arithmetic/e4m3-rewrite-normalize.svg" alt="" aria-hidden="true">
</div>
:::

::: {.e4m3-rewrite-copy data-id="e4m3-copy"}
<div class="e4m3-stage-cue stage-exponent">Then: encode the exponent.</div>

Let $E$ be the stored exponent field and $B=7$ its bias. The exponent used by
the real value is $e=E-B$.

::: {.e4m3-stage-math .stage-exponent}
$$\begin{aligned}
e_r &= (E_a-B)+(E_b-B)+n \\
E_r &= e_r+B \\
    &= E_a+E_b-B+n
\end{aligned}$$
:::

Adding the two stored fields counts the bias twice. Encoding the result adds
one bias back, so the circuit subtracts only one bias overall.
:::
::::

$$E_r=E_a+E_b-7+n$$

Use five-bit intermediates to preserve the carry while adding the stored
exponents, removing one bias, and applying the normalization correction.

```python-circt
eb5 = comb.ConcatOp.create(zero1, eb).result
```

## One operation, many circuits {#arithmetic-hardware-freedom}

`arith.mulf` specifies a numerical operation. It does not prescribe one
microarchitecture.

::: {.incremental}
- Use a generic IEEE-style multiplier, or exploit one small format.

- Choose rounding, exception handling, latency, and target technology.

- Trade a multiplier for a lookup table when the domain is tiny.

- Recognize stronger intent: a square, a constant product, or a fused graph.
:::

This **hardware freedom** is the design space studied in computer-arithmetic
books, papers, and venues such as the
[IEEE Symposium on Computer Arithmetic](https://www.arithsymposium.org/)
[@dinechin2024asa, ch. 14-15].

## Quiz: should `%x * %x` cost the same? {#arithmetic-square-quiz}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="48%"}
**Generic product**

```mlir
%p = arith.mulf %a, %b : f8E4M3FN
```
:::

::: {.column width="48%"}
**Square**

```mlir
%p = arith.mulf %x, %x : f8E4M3FN
```
:::
::::

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon=false}
## What becomes simpler when both SSA operands are identical?
:::

::: {.incremental}
1. $s_x \oplus s_x = 0$: the normal finite result is positive.
2. $E_x + E_x = 2E_x$: one exponent is decoded and doubled.
3. The significand partial-product matrix is symmetric.
:::

## The product matrix contains repeated work {#arithmetic-square-matrix}

![](assets/images/arithmetic/square-partial-products.svg){fig-alt="Comparison of the sixteen partial products in a generic four-bit multiplier with the six unique cross products and four diagonal wires in a four-bit squarer" width="88%" fig-align="center"}

For a square, the lower triangle duplicates the upper triangle and the
diagonal does not require an AND gate [@dinechin2024asa, sec. 14.2].

## Why the significand squarer is cheaper {#arithmetic-square-derivation}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="46%"}
For $X=\sum_i 2^i x_i$:

$$
X^2 = \sum_i 2^{2i}x_i
    + \sum_{j<i} 2^{i+j+1}x_ix_j
$$
:::

::: {.column width="54%"}
::: {.incremental}
- **Diagonal:** $x_i x_i=x_i$, so it is a wire.
- **Mirror:** $x_ix_j=x_jx_i$, so compute the pair once and shift its weight.
- **Four bits:** 16 generic partial products become 6 ANDs and 4 wires.
:::
:::
::::

The bit complexity is roughly halved before compression and rounding. The
floating-point normalization and exceptional-value policy remain.

`build_square4` emits the six unique cross products and routes the four

## Exercise 8 (optional): build the 4-bit squarer {#arithmetic-square-builder}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="39%"}
For each input bit $x_i$:

- route $x_i$ directly to bit position $2i$;
- compute $x_i x_j$ once for every $j<i$;
- place that cross product at bit position $i+j+1$.

The loop describes the bit heap. Constant shifts become wiring, and the
generic `comb.add` network can be compressed by synthesis.
:::

::: {.column width="61%"}
```python-circt
def build_square4(x):
    bits = [
        comb.ExtractOp.create(i, i1, x).result
        for i in range(4)
    ]
    zero7 = hw.ConstantOp.create(i7, 0).result

    def at_weight(bit, weight):
        wide = comb.ConcatOp.create(zero7, bit).result
        shift = hw.ConstantOp.create(i8, weight).result
        return comb.ShlOp.create(wide, shift).result

    terms = [at_weight(bits[i], 2 * i) for i in range(4)]
    for i in range(4):
        for j in range(i):
            cross = comb.AndOp.create(bits[i], bits[j]).result
            terms.append(at_weight(cross, i + j + 1))

    return comb.AddOp.create(*terms).result
```
:::
::::

## Match more intent; build better datapaths {#arithmetic-specialization-opening}

The same rewrite strategy extends beyond one squarer:

| Recognized arithmetic | Possible datapath |
|---|---|
| `%x * %x` | dedicated squarer |
| `%x * C` | constant multiplier or shift-add network |
| `%a * %b + %c` | fused multiply-add with one final rounding |
| $\sum_i x_i^2$ | fused sum-of-squares datapath |
| dot product or polynomial | target-sized fused operator |

::: {.fragment}
